title: The coefficient setting: six operations only
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, a power $q=p^a$, the fields $k_0=\Fq$ and $k=\bar k_0$, a
prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with algebraic closure
$\Qlb$. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k_0$. We use:
the bounded constructible derived category $D^b_c(-,E)$ — the adic
category, $\Dbc$ of the pro-étale $E$-sheaves of the six-functor package
(derived-complete $\mathcal O_E$-complexes of étale origin, rationalized),
*not* the derived category of discrete sheaves of $E$-modules on the small
étale site, on which the base-change isomorphisms fail — with the six operations $Lf^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,Rf^!,\otimes^L, R\mathcal H om$ in the form of the six-functor package, the
compact-support direct image $Rf_!=Rf_*\circ j_!$ read through a
compactification, ordinary and compact-support cohomology, and the Tate
twists. The additive character $\psi$ takes values in
$\mu_p\subset\Qlb^\times$, so the Artin–Schreier sheaf and the Fourier
kernel $\mathcal K_\psi$ are a priori $\Qlb$-sheaves; we assume throughout
that $\mu_p\subset E$, so that $\psi$ is $E$-valued, $\mathcal K_\psi$ is a
lisse $E$-sheaf of rank one, and the tensor product $\otimes^L_E$ in the
definition of the transform makes sense on $\Dbc(V,E)$. (Without this
assumption the transform is defined at the $\Qlb$-stage, or over $E(\mu_p)$
after extension of scalars.) No weight, no $L^2$-weight parameter and no purity notion is used
anywhere in this file; the Tate twist is a coefficient normalization (the
blueprint records its definition among the weight foundations, but no weight
statement of that chapter is used below).

reviewed_lean.note: FourierSetting matches the source setting, uses real inherited coefficient declarations, has complete docstrings/report sections, covers edge cases, and compiles cleanly with scompile.py.
